title: Furious pace of AI investment on some Fed officials' radar now
excerpt: Federal Reserve officials are beginning to mull whether the frenzied investment driving the buildout of the artificial intelligence sector is getting out of...
content_html:
By Michael S. Derby

Aug 6 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve officials are beginning to mull whether the frenzied investment driving the buildout of the artificial intelligence sector is getting out of hand and creating risks for the financial sector.

For now, some ‌of the officials who have tackled the subject call for vigilance, dashed with a sense that a financial crisis mirroring ‌what happened 20 years ago with housing, and to a lesser degree, the dot-com shakeout before that, is probably not in the offing. Still, the scale of investment, ​the uncertain returns for an unproven technology, the rise of tricky financing structures and increased use of debt have moved AI finance onto central bankers' radar.

"I don't see this as a bubble kind of situation," Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said in an interview with Reuters conducted on Friday.

"What we're seeing is a very high level of excitement, enthusiasm around new technology, around AI," Williams said. "Investors are trying in ‌real time to solve an almost intractable problem, and ⁠that is how big are the benefits of AI going to prove to be," and trying to answer these questions will lead to volatility.

Williams said that while there's been an increase in borrowing to support the ⁠AI investment it is being managed by companies with high earnings, noting, "I'm not as worried about the financial stability from the leverage right now."

Torsten Slok, chief economist at money manager Apollo, said in a research note, "The data-center buildout is still less than half the size of the housing boom, which ​peaked ​at 6.6% of GDP in 2005," while at the same time the investment ​pace relative to GDP has been growing faster than ‌housing did in the run up to the global financial crisis.

MONITORING TIME

Others on the Fed appear less sanguine about AI risk relative to Williams.

Given how the industry is financing itself "I would argue that, that there's some signs that we have to really start to talk about that on a macro level, is this industry becoming another too big to fail?" asked Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid in a speech on Tuesday.

In particular, he's worried about the flow of financing and how the linkages could be a vector where a problem starts at one ‌stage and then propagates.

Schmid asked, "Does the does the circular motion of a commitment, ​let's say a contractual commitment to a data center to an energy provider … ​to a community that it serves, is that, is that circle ​getting too leveraged? And if you get a spark that starts a flame, what happens?"

content_html_zh:
作者：迈克尔·S. 德比

路透 8 月 6 日 - 美联储官员开始思考，推动人工智能行业发展的疯狂投资是否正在失控，并给金融行业带来风险。

目前，一些处理这一问题的官员呼吁保持警惕，他们感到，类似 20 年前房地产市场的金融危机，以及之前的互联网泡沫的洗牌，可能不会很快发生。 尽管如此，投资规模、未经证实的技术的不确定回报、棘手的融资结构的兴起以及债务使用的增加已经将人工智能金融纳入了央行行长的关注范围。

纽约联邦储备银行行长约翰·威廉姆斯在周五接受路透社采访时表示：“我不认为这是一种泡沫情况。”

威廉姆斯说：“我们看到的是人们对新技术、人工智能的高度兴奋和热情。” “投资者正在尝试实时解决一个几乎棘手的问题，这就是人工智能的好处将被证明有多大”，而试图回答这些问题将导致波动。

威廉姆斯表示，虽然支持人工智能投资的借款有所增加，但这些投资是由高收益公司管理的，并指出，“我现在并不担心杠杆带来的财务稳定性。”

资金管理公司 Apollo 的首席经济学家 Torsten Slok 在一份研究报告中表示，“数据中心的建设规模仍不到房地产繁荣规模的一半，房地产繁荣在 2005 年达到顶峰，占 GDP 的 6.6%”，而与此同时，相对于 GDP 的投资速度增长速度快于全球金融危机爆发前的房地产增长速度。

监控时间

与威廉姆斯相比，美联储的其他成员似乎对人工智能风险不那么乐观。

考虑到该行业如何为自身融资，“我认为，有一些迹象表明我们必须真正开始在宏观层面上讨论这个问题，这个行业是否会成为另一个大而不能倒的行业？” 堪萨斯城联储主席杰夫·施密德在周二的讲话中问道。

他特别担心融资的流动，以及这种联系如何成为问题在某个阶段开始然后蔓延的载体。

施密德问道：“承诺的循环运动，比方说对数据中心的合同承诺，对能源提供商……对其所服务的社区的承诺，是不是，这个圈子的杠杆作用是否太大了？ 如果你得到一个火花，点燃火焰，会发生什么？”
